Asser S, Bitarakwate E, Gill M, Hoffman HJ, Musana O, Phiri A, and colleagues conducted a study on the implementation of rapid syphilis testing within programs aimed at preventing mother-to-child transmission of HIV in Uganda and Zambia. This research focused on evaluating the acceptability and feasibility of introducing such testing in field settings. The findings were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2012, volume 61, pages e40–e46. 2. Vickerman P, Peeling RW, Terris-Prestholt F, Changalucha J, Mabey D, Watson-Jones D, and Watts C developed a model to assess the cost-effectiveness of incorporating rapid syphilis tests into antenatal syphilis screening programs in Mwanza, Tanzania. Their work, which analyzed the economic and health impacts of this intervention, was published in the journal Sexually Transmitted Infections in 2006, volume 82 (Supplement 5), pages v38–v43.
